q-233241.name: Question 1
q-233241.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{3}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x-2} & ={5}^{4x} \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{x-2}) & ={log}_{3}⁡({5}^{4x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
x-2={log}_{3}⁡({5}^{4x}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-2=4x{log}_{3}⁡(5)
$$

Then, we solve for $x,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =4x{log}_{3}⁡(5) \\ x & =2+4x{log}_{3}⁡(5) \\ x-4x{log}_{3}⁡(5) & =2 \\ x(1-4{log}_{3}⁡(5)) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{1-4{log}_{3}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{3}⁡(5)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}≈1.464\,974.
$$

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as

$$
x≈\frac{2}{1-4(1.464\,974)}≈-0.412,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

q-98908.problem: Given that ${3}^{x}={2}^{x-1},$ what is the value of $x?$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
q-98908.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{3}$ on both sides of the equation: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x} & ={2}^{x-1} \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{x}) & ={log}_{3}⁡({2}^{x-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={log}_{3}⁡({2}^{x-1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x-1){log}_{3}⁡(2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x-1){log}_{3}⁡(2) \\ x & =x{log}_{3}⁡(2)-{log}_{3}⁡(2) \\ x-x{log}_{3}⁡(2) & =-{log}_{3}⁡(2) \\ x(1-{log}_{3}⁡(2)) & =-{log}_{3}⁡(2) \\ x & =-\frac{{log}_{3}⁡(2)}{1-{log}_{3}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the change of base formula, we have

$$
{log}_{3}⁡(2)=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}≈0.630\,930.
$$

Finally, we can approximate $x$ as

$$
x≈-\frac{0.630\,930}{1-0.630\,930}≈-1.710,
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

q-66897.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-5}={4}^{x}?$
q-66897.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-5} & ={4}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-5}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-5 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡4 & =5 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡4) & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\end{aligned}
$$

q-66896.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x-1}={3}^{x}?$
q-66896.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-1} & ={3}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-1 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡3 & =1 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =1 \\ x & =\frac{1}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

1−ln⁡3
b
11−ln⁡3

1−ln⁡33

ln⁡2−ln⁡3
e
log⁡31+ln⁡3

First, we take the natural logarithm (ln) of both sides of the equation:

ex−1=3xln⁡(ex−1)=ln⁡(3x)

Now, we use the fact that ln⁡(ea)=a to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

x−1=ln⁡(3x)

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

x−1=xln⁡3

Finally, we solve for x, as follows:

x−1=xln⁡3x−xln⁡3=1x(1−ln⁡3)=1x=11−ln⁡3

q-242902.name: Question 5
q-242902.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2} & ={2}^{x+3} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x+2=\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+3}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x+2=(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =(x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x+2 & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2 \\ x & =\frac{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)-2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)}\end{aligned}
$$

q-100469.name: Question 6
q-100469.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x+4} & ={6}^{2-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{x+4}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{2-3x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2-3x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x & =\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$

q-242923.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{2x} & ={8}^{1-6x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({3}^{2x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{1-6x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(1-6x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+6x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8))}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(4-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)=(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8).

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

\begin{aligned}(4-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =(2x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) & =2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ -x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ x & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
